claim: For the ferromagnetic Blum–Kapel model on the Cayley tree of order \(2\), use the source parameter \(\lambda=e^{J/T}>1\) and its positive translation-invariant boundary-law system. Define \(p(\lambda)=4\lambda^4+7\lambda^3-14\lambda^2-33\lambda-12\), and let \(\lambda_c\) be its unique positive root. Then \(\lambda_c=2.1028158432915363745\ldots\), the boundary-law system has exactly one positive solution for \(1<\lambda\le\lambda_c\), and exactly three positive solutions for \(\lambda>\lambda_c\). The two additional solutions are interchanged by the spin symmetry. Hence the critical coupling reported in the source as \(\lambda_{cr}\approx2.1132163\) is not the actual translation-invariant bifurcation point; the corrected critical temperature is \(T_c=J/\log \lambda_c\).

correctness.rationale: Taking positive square roots of the published order-\(2\) fixed-point system is reversible. The symmetric branch is unique because \(2x+x^{-1}-x^{-2}\) is strictly increasing. Every nonsymmetric solution reduces to a positive root \(u\) of \(u^2-(\lambda+\lambda^{-1})u+(\lambda-1)/(\lambda+1)=0\) with \(D=2(\lambda-\lambda^{-1})u-u^2-2>0\). The lower root always has \(D<0\). The upper root has \(D=0\) exactly when \(p(\lambda)=0\); Descartes' rule and the signs at \(2\) and \(3\) give one positive critical root. The sign change yields exactly zero or two nonsymmetric solutions on the two sides. The packaged checker verifies the algebraic identities, a rational isolating interval, and direct residuals of reconstructed solutions.
